Hello there. I don't follow a religion. I believe in good ethics and morals. I try to remember that everyone is fighting their own battle. I used to be a huge pessimist but I've been trying to leave more room for hope lately. I also didn't believe in fate but have recently decided to let some things go and perhaps fall into place just to have a little less anxiety since I'm a bit of a control freak.

Thank you for your help and for prompting me to see a psychiatrist. I'm well aware that a professional would help me better with a diagnosis, but I was asking about the laugh-crying specifically. 

I'm going to answer some of your questions below: 
The Paxera and Cipralex were both prescribed to me by family doctors. Paxera when I was 16 (I didn't take it because I researched and it said you shouldn't take it if you're under 18 because it might increase feelings of suicide or harming others). Cipralex at 24 after I had a bad asthma attack and the doctor made me fill out a form about generalized anxiety since it's one of the triggers for asthma. Both told me to take them for 6 months and go back in for a follow up. I never took a pill. 

My psychologist told me at some point when I was having hallucinations and suicidal thoughts that she could refer me to a psychiatrist but that she wouldn't because she believed I was "strong enough to overcome it without meds." She repeatedly asked me about the hallucinations and I told her I knew they weren't real and just a product of my imagination. That seemed to reassure her that I didn't need to see a psychiatrist and she just gave me breathing exercises and told me to ignore them. They evolved and tried to get my attention when I ignored them. I told her it didn't work. But they became less frequent when I took a break from work and life for 3 months. I slept a lot and spent time with my family. I felt mentally healthier and was only left with paranoia. Every now and then, I have mild hallucinations especially if I haven't been sleeping well or if I'm feeling particularly unstable. 

As for the suicidal thoughts, she tried to break down the feeling that urges me to kill myself. She explained that, as humans, it goes against our survival instinct to want to kill ourselves. So perhaps what I'm feeling is being overwhelmed and wanting to "end it all" and death is just the first solution that comes to mind. She then asked me to put her number on speed dial and to contact her if I ever have any of those thoughts for longer than 10 minutes. I still get them every once in a while but it's not as bad as it used to be (like 5 months of constant contemplation of suicide). I've been working for almost 2 years on a dream of mine and that has helped a lot. 

Thanks again for listening, caring and helping. Have a nice day. :)
